extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary critics, and aspiring writers interested in poetic theory and craft
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and critical guidance for composing and judging poetry: definitions of poem/poetry, distinctions between imagination and fancy, and specific symptoms of original poetic genius (musicality, imagery, subject-choice, depth of thought, unity, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary vs Secondary Imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary Imagination is the living power and prime agent of all human perception, a repetition in the finite mind of the eternal act of creation; the secondary Imagination is an echo of the former, co-existing with the conscious will and identical in kind but differing in degree and mode of operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary Imagination is generative and unifying (dissolves, diffuses, recreates); the secondary idealizes and unifies from received materials. Treating imagination as active, synthetic power distinguishes genuine poetic creation from mere mechanical invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fancy vs Imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Fancy is a mode of memory emancipated from time and space and receives all materials ready-made from association; it deals with fixities and definites. Imagination dissolves and recreates, striving to idealize and unify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'fancy' when recombining preformed images/memories; rely on 'imagination' when transforming and giving life and unity to disparate materials. Avoid confusing technical memory-play (fancy) with formative creative synthesis (imagination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Poem's immediate object — pleasure not truth
rubrics_metrics.description: A poem, in the strictest sense, proposes for its immediate object pleasure, not truth; it is distinguished from works of science by this immediate end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While ultimate truth or moral may be present, the poem's craft must aim to give pleasure through its whole and parts. Pleasure must be grounded in reasons within the poem (not mere ornament).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct gratification from each component part
rubrics_metrics.description: A poem should provide such delight from the whole as is compatible with a distinct gratification from each component part (meter, line, image).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each line/part must justify attention and contribute to sustained pleasure; metre/rhyme must be consonant with content so the reader can take pleasure both in parts and in the whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity and mutual support of parts
rubrics_metrics.description: A legitimate poem's parts must mutually support and explain each other; they should harmonize with, and support, the purpose and influences of metrical arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid collections of striking lines that each stand alone; design parts to interrelate so the poem reads as an organic, unified whole rather than disconnected epigrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustain continuous and equal attention (reader's pleasurable journey)
rubrics_metrics.description: The poem should excite a more continuous and equal attention than prose aims at; the reader should be carried forward by the pleasure of the journey itself, not merely curiosity about the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft progression, pacing, and attractions so the reader delights at every step; balance surprise and continuity to maintain engagement rather than abrupt 'teasing' toward an end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unsustained composition and disjoined couplets
rubrics_metrics.description: A poem should not be a series of striking lines or distiches each absorbing attention to itself and becoming a separate whole, nor an unsustained composition where the reader only gathers the general result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure cohesion and cumulative effect; guard against writing that reads as a string of memorable lines lacking connective purpose or development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versification and musical sweetness
rubrics_metrics.description: Perfect sweetness of versification and the musical delight of sound, adapted to the subject and varying the march of words without inappropriate loftiness, is a primary excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate original richness and sweetness of sound (not mere mechanical devices). Versification must suit the poem's thought and mood; musical gifts are a sign of imagination rather than mere technical skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metre/rhyme must justify content
rubrics_metrics.description: If metre or rhyme is superadded to a composition, all other parts must be made consonant with it; metre should justify the perpetual attention the form demands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using formal metrical structures, shape diction, syntax, and imagery to serve them so that metrical repetition enhances rather than conflicts with meaning and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of subject — distance from personal circumstance
rubrics_metrics.description: A promise of genius is choosing subjects remote from the private interests and circumstances of the writer; subjects too immediately from personal sensation often give equivocal marks of genius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer subjects that reveal imaginative reach and empathy beyond autobiographical material; objectivity and the ability to present other lives convincingly are marks of maturity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet's detachment (alienation from passions depicted)
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet often remains unparticipating in the passions he depicts, placing characters and scenes before the reader while his own feelings are aloof, allowing rich imagery and reflection to modulate sympathy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain critical distance to prevent endorsing base impulses; let depiction and commentary balance to prevent simple voyeuristic or indulgent presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery integrated by predominant passion
rubrics_metrics.description: Images, however beautiful, become proofs of original genius only when modified by a predominant passion, associated thoughts, reduction of multitude to unity, or by imparting human and intellectual life from the poet's spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't rely on isolated pretty images; shape imagery so it springs from and reinforces the central feeling or idea, and so creates simultaneity or unity of effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery molds to circumstance and character
rubrics_metrics.description: Imagery attains highest value when it molds and colours itself to the circumstances, passion, or character present and foremost in the mind, supplying dignity and passion to objects presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and adapt images to the poem's mood and personae; imagery should illuminate character and situation rather than merely decorate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth and energy of thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Depth and intellectual energy of thought are necessary: no great poet has been without being at the same time a profound philosopher; poetry is the blossom of all human knowledge and thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate learning and reflective power; intellectual substance must underlie imaginative display so that creative power and thought balance and sustain each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance and reconciliation of opposites (synthesizing faculties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetic Imagination reveals itself in the balance or reconcilement of opposite qualities: sameness with difference, general with concrete, idea with image, individual with representative, novelty with familiarity, emotion with order, judgment with enthusiasm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for synthesis rather than mere juxtaposition: unite contrasts into a coherent effect. The poet's craft lies in subordinating art to nature and manner to matter while fusing faculties into unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language appropriate to subject (ordinary language for ordinary subjects)
rubrics_metrics.description: For subjects drawn from ordinary life, language of ordinary life may be employed so as to awaken attention to the loveliness and wonders of the everyday without extraneous ornament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match diction to subject-matter: simple colloquial speech can produce poetic effect when it helps elicit sympathy and novelty; avoid unnatural ornament that obscures the poem's intention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Studied selection and artificial arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: To preserve parts in keeping with the poetry, a studied selection and artificial arrangement is required; selection and arrangement partake of the property of exciting continuous attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately select material and order it to maintain poetic unity and attention; arrangement is part of poetic craft and should support the poem's proportional harmony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic faith — willing suspension of disbelief
rubrics_metrics.description: For supernatural or romantic subjects, achieve a human interest and semblance of truth sufficient to procure the willing suspension of disbelief which constitutes poetic faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When invoking the uncanny or supernatural, ground emotion and behavior in psychological truth so readers accept the fiction for the poem's duration; plausibility within feeling is key.
